attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, written as a firm narrative assertion.

semantics.note: Keeps 'just about every', 'had to' and the timing after June 2025. This is a past-tense observation.

contract.note: Plain reading is ordinary: austerity means price increases, tighter limits or cuts, applied to nearly all AI app startups from June 2025 to March 2026. Requiring a prevalence record, and evidence of necessity for 'had to', is fair.

evidence.note: Cursor disclosure dated June 2025: moved from request-based pricing to a capped usage allowance. Supports one named example only, not prevalence.
Augment Code moved to credits in Oct 2025. Page available before the evaluation date. One more example; not prevalence.
Replit's effort-based pricing lowered charges for simple tasks, which qualifies the austerity framing. It neither proves nor disproves prevalence.
May 2026 survey of planned future pricing changes. Different period and outcome; context only.

reviews.rationale: The packet has a few company examples of tighter pricing (Cursor, Augment) and one mixed case (Replit). Nothing shows that nearly all AI startups adopted austerity, and nothing shows the cuts were necessary. Selected examples cannot establish the 'just about every' quantifier, so the evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will have to' is an unhedged forecast. Keeps both companies, 'massively' and the open-ended 'at some point'.

contract.note: Reading the claim as large cuts to included subscription usage at both companies, driven by economics, is ordinary and fair. With no deadline, the forecast can only resolve on a conclusive event.

evidence.note: Reports peak-hour limits and third-party access blocks at Anthropic around late March 2026. Covers one company only and is not a clearly massive comparable cut.
Anthropic doubled Claude Code limits in May 2026. Cuts in the other direction, but this cannot disprove eventual cuts.
OpenAI raised Codex limits and paused new Pro sign-ups. A sign-up pause is not an allowance cut.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. No conclusive event shows large, economically driven allowance cuts at both companies. The evidence is mixed: Anthropic restricted usage and then raised limits, and OpenAI raised limits. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

semantics.note: Keeps 'invariably', the short-term revenue gain and the push toward cheaper open models and failure. This is a general causal claim.

contract.note: Mostly fair. The contract flags that 'push toward' may mean pressure rather than completed failure. Under either reading the packet cannot settle the claim.

evidence.note: Lindy moved traffic from Claude to cheaper DeepSeek and cut inference costs. The packet does not tie this to supplier price hikes, show supplier revenue gains, or show any business failure.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is one startup that switched to a cheaper model, which the packet does not link to OpenAI or Anthropic price hikes. Nothing shows supplier revenue gains, systematic migration or failure, so the causal 'invariably' claim cannot be judged on this record.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition drops the second clause, that more intensive work makes outputs more expensive, although the contract includes it. Otherwise it is a fair general observation.

contract.note: Reading it as a general link between usage and provider serving cost is ordinary. The speaker did not choose February 2026 as the period or serving cost as the metric, and the result turns on those choices.

evidence.note: OpenAI Sept 2025: the model spends more tokens on complex tasks. This is a mechanism, not customer cost data, and predates the target period.
July 2025 report of one subscriber using tens of thousands of dollars of usage on a $200 plan. Usage value is not serving cost, the period is wrong, and there is no comparison across users.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no customer-level serving-cost data for the target period. The items show that complex tasks use more compute and that heavy users exist, but not the measured relationship the contract requires. Unresolved on this record.
